title: Sentinel error types for category rendering.
status: DONE 2026-05-15: ErrUnreachable/ErrTimeout/ErrBadAddress/ErrUnknownParameter/ErrParameterReadOnly/ErrWriteRejected/ErrTransportNotSupported/ErrInvalidArgument live in mecom/errors.go with errors_test.go pinning each.
spec: Goal: add typed sentinel errors that a frontend can match on. Required work: introduce ErrUnreachable, ErrTimeout, ErrBadAddress, ErrUnknownParameter, ErrParameterReadOnly, ErrWriteRejected, ErrTransportNotSupported in package mecom; wrap existing fmt.Errorf sites at write/read/factory boundaries with errors.Join or %w so errors.Is keeps working; add table-driven test asserting each sentinel surfaces from its trigger path. Acceptance: a consumer can write `errors.Is(err, mecom.ErrUnreachable)` and get a stable boolean across transports; godoc lists every sentinel; tests pin each one.
order_note: Foundational - the gateway and lease both need these for status mapping. Cheapest item, unblocks the rest.

title: Telemetry subscription primitive (mecom.Subscriber).
status: DONE 2026-05-15: mecom.Subscriber + NewSubscriber + C()/Run(ctx) ship in mecom/subscriber.go; tests cover ok/nan/unreachable quality.
spec: Goal: wrap mecom.Readout.Poll into a push primitive so consumers receive Telemetry events on a channel instead of running their own loops. Required work: in package mecom, add type Subscriber with constructor NewSubscriber(client ReadClient, params []Parameter, interval time.Duration) and methods Run(ctx) error + C() <-chan tmtc.Telemetry; convert each ReadoutValue from Readout.Poll into one tmtc.Telemetry per signal with TargetID, Name, Unit, Time, Value, Quality; on read error mark Quality=unreachable but keep streaming. Add unit test using a scripted ReadClient that asserts N parameters produce N telemetry events per cycle. Acceptance: gateway and any future Go consumer can consume `for tm := range sub.C() { ... }` without building their own poll loop.
order_note: Highest leverage missing piece. The HTTP/WS gateway is just a transport over this channel.

title: Write-authority lease primitive (mecom/writelease).
status: DONE 2026-05-15: package mecom/writelease with Acquire/Release/Validate/List + sentinel errors; mecom.Commander.Authorizer gates writes when set.
spec: Goal: provide a small lease registry that gates writes/control on an opaque token. Required work: new package mecom/writelease with WriteLease{DeviceID, Holder, Token, ExpiresAt}, Registry with Acquire(deviceID, holder, ttl) (WriteLease, error), Release(token) error, Validate(deviceID, token) error, List() []WriteLease; expirations swept on each call; goroutine-safe. Add an optional Authorizer hook on mecom.Commander so Send() consults a lease before dispatching write_* or reset/save; reads always allowed. Document that the lease is advisory inside the library - the gateway will enforce it on the wire. Test: two acquires for same device serialize; second gets ErrLeaseHeld; expired lease releases automatically. Acceptance: consumers can require a token for writes without changing the wire protocol; default Commander behaviour unchanged unless Authorizer is wired in.
order_note: Authority gate must exist as a primitive before any gateway exposes write endpoints.

title: Connection-state surface on mecomserver.
status: DONE 2026-05-15: BrokerStats (Connected/LastConnectAt/LastErrorAt/FramesIn/FramesOut/ErrorCount) + RouterConfig.Stats(); tests cover connect path and dial-error path.
spec: Goal: expose per-route status so a UI status pill can render. Required work: in mecomserver, add type BrokerStats{Address, Target, Connected bool, LastConnectAt time.Time, LastErrorAt time.Time, LastError string, FramesIn uint64, FramesOut uint64, ErrorCount uint64}; runBroker updates the struct via a *atomic*-protected snapshot; expose RouterConfig.StatsSnapshot() map[byte]BrokerStats; same for HubConfig hub-level aggregation. Add test that brings up a router with one route, exercises one successful and one failed downstream dial, then asserts FramesIn/ErrorCount/LastError. Acceptance: a UI can call StatsSnapshot once per second and render a per-device status line without poking at internals.
order_note: Required for status pills and health endpoints; cheap because the data already passes through the broker.

title: HTTP/SSE gateway (cmd/mecomgw).
spec: Goal: bundle an HTTP gateway that fronts mecomvseriald (or direct devices) with a UI-friendly surface. Required work: new cmd/mecomgw exposing GET /api/devices (catalogue + last-seen via BrokerStats), GET /api/catalogue (mecomdict parameter table), POST /api/devices/{id}/lease (acquire write lease), DELETE /api/devices/{id}/lease (release), POST /api/devices/{id}/write (write_float32/write_int32/reset/save_to_flash, requires lease token), GET /api/devices/{id}/poll?params=...&interval=... (Server-Sent Events of Telemetry), GET /ws/stream (WebSocket equivalent of poll for multi-device subscription). Reuses mecom.NewForEndpoint, mecom.Subscriber, mecom.Commander, writelease.Registry; one process per deployment. Add a JSON config (or flags) for backend targets. Acceptance: a curl against /api/devices returns JSON; a wscat /ws/stream subscription receives Telemetry events; writes without a valid lease token return 423 Locked.
order_note: The bridge between library and browser. Lands after the three primitives so it is mostly glue. WebSocket /ws/stream deferred - SSE /poll is functionally equivalent for our needs.

title: Gateway OpenAPI / TypeScript types.
status: DONE 2026-05-15: docs/gateway/openapi.yaml + docs/gateway/types.d.ts + cmd/mecomgw/openapi_test.go enforces handler-parity in CI.
spec: Goal: publish a machine-readable description of the gateway endpoints. Required work: add docs/gateway/openapi.yaml describing every /api and /ws route from id 5, with request and response schemas referencing mecom.Parameter, tmtc.Telemetry, tmtc.CommandEvent, BrokerStats, WriteLease; add a small Go test that loads the OpenAPI file and asserts every handler in cmd/mecomgw is referenced; generate a tracked TypeScript types file under docs/gateway/types.d.ts for direct frontend consumption. Acceptance: contributors can regenerate types from one source; UI prototypes do not duplicate field names; CI fails when a gateway handler is added without an OpenAPI entry.
order_note: Last because it describes a finished surface; doing it before id 5 freezes the schema prematurely.

title: Graph-wall and signal-dictionary UI contract.
status: DONE 2026-05-15: docs/gateway/UI_GRAPH_WALL_CONTRACT.md defines the SignalForge-aligned signal hierarchy, default temperature/power hero graphs, telecommand cards, command activity fields, channel roles, mock/live boundaries, and QA gates for the design agent.
spec: Goal: give frontend/design agents a repo-backed contract for the richer Meerstetter operator UI without inventing backend endpoints. Required work: document the hierarchy signal group / signal subgroup / signal / device / instance; pin default graph assignments for target/object/sink/cascade temperatures and voltage/current/power channels; document writable command-card behavior and command activity provenance; distinguish live API, client-side assignment state, and planned backend surfaces. Acceptance: design work can reuse SignalForge graphwall/graphsem concepts and Gossamer visual patterns while keeping cmd/mecomgw/openapi.yaml as the live API truth.
order_note: Unblocks Claude/design work while keeping the public API boundary explicit.

title: Enrich gateway catalogue for signal dictionary rows.
spec: Goal: make /api/catalogue carry enough structured metadata for the UI hierarchy without browser-side inference. Required work: include or map SignalForge graphsem/source-catalogue fields such as group/category, subgroup, signal ID, display name, role, kind, unit, writable access, device family, preferred graph aggregate, and default instance policy. Preserve backwards-compatible fields already in GatewayCatalogueEntry. Acceptance: the frontend can build telemetry and telecommand dictionary trees from one catalogue response, with no hardcoded parameter ID tables except graceful fallback labels.
order_note: Needed after the design contract so the implementation can become live-data driven.

title: Command activity event stream/history.
spec: Goal: every staged or committed telecommand should be visible in the UI and exportable. Required work: define a gateway command-event shape with command ID, timestamp, device, instance, parameter, previous value if known, requested value, unit, lease holder, endpoint provenance, status, and error category/message. Expose a short live stream or recent-history endpoint and wire write handlers to publish accepted/sent/acked/completed/rejected/failed transitions. Acceptance: command cards and graph markers can render exact provenance and status without scraping HTTP responses.
order_note: Required for trustworthy telecommand UX and exact command markers.

title: Graph assignment persistence and export contract.
spec: Goal: preserve which signal appears in which graph and which telecommand appears in which command card. Required work: define a small JSON contract aligned with SignalForge graphwall TileConfig and Assignment, covering wall_id, tile_id, kind, target_id, position, options, device, instance, and command-card placement. Start client-side, then expose import/export through gateway or archive once storage exists. Acceptance: operators can modify graph and command-card assignments, reload the UI, and export graph_wall_assignments with parseable provenance.
order_note: Keeps the graph wall configurable without coupling it to one frontend implementation.

title: Ring-buffer history and archive endpoints.
spec: Goal: make the graph wall show useful recent history from Pi RAM ring, Pi flash fallback ring, and TEC internal ring buffers when available. Required work: define history/replay endpoint contracts, duplicate suppression keys, source precedence, time alignment, and export formats for telemetry_samples, can_frames, command_events, object_dictionary_snapshots, and graph_wall_assignments. Acceptance: late UI connection can bootstrap from recent history, then switch to live SSE without duplicate points or pretending planned storage is live.
order_note: Completes the live/historical UX after catalogue and command provenance are structured.

title: Claude Design operator console artifact imported.
status: DONE 2026-05-15: docs/gateway/console contains the dense operator-console prototype with SignalForge-style hero graphs, signal dictionary hierarchy, bottom telemetry/telecommand accordions, mock/live gateway switch, and contract-aligned parameter IDs.
spec: Goal: preserve the Claude Design work in-repo and make it serve through cmd/mecomgw -ui-dir. Acceptance: /ui/ loads the console via docs/gateway/console/index.html, mock mode works without hardware, and the handoff bundle includes the console files.
order_note: Keeps the design artifact reviewable and shareable from the repository while backend live bindings mature.

title: Productionize operator console live bindings.
spec: Goal: replace prototype-local inference with live gateway data once ids 8-11 land. Required work: drive dictionary rows from enriched /api/catalogue, consume command activity history/stream, load graph assignments and ring-buffer history from backend contracts, and remove mock-only fallbacks from production mode. Acceptance: the console can run against four live TEC controllers over the PiXtend CAN route with no hardcoded parameter tables beyond graceful labels.
order_note: Follow-up after the UI shell is preserved; separates prototype import from hardware-backed production behavior.
